cobra.definition: Venomous Asiatic and African elapid snakes that can expand the skin of the neck into a hood.

python.definition: (Greek mythology) dragon killed by Apollo at Delphi.

rattlesnake.definition: Pit viper with horny segments at the end of the tail that rattle when shaken.

boa.definition: A long thin fluffy scarf of feathers or fur.

viper.definition: Venomous Old World snakes characterized by hollow venom-conducting fangs in the upper jaw.

corn-snake.definition: A nonvenomous North American snake with orange, reddish, or brown blotched coloring, commonly kept in zoological collections and as a pet.
corn-snake.exampleUsage: The corn snake rested beneath a shelter in the exhibit.

king-snake.definition: A nonvenomous snake of the genus Lampropeltis, known for eating a varied diet that can include other snakes.
king-snake.exampleUsage: The king snake moved slowly across its enclosure.

anaconda.definition: Large arboreal boa of tropical South America.

mamba.definition: Arboreal snake of central and southern Africa whose bite is often fatal.

garter-snake.definition: A generally small, slender North American snake of the genus Thamnophis, often marked with lengthwise stripes.
garter-snake.exampleUsage: A garter snake was visible near the water feature.

gecko.definition: Any of various small chiefly tropical and usually nocturnal insectivorous terrestrial lizards typically with immovable eyelids.
gecko.exampleUsage: The gecko was identified during the lesson.

iguana.definition: Large herbivorous tropical American arboreal lizards with a spiny crest along the back.

chameleon.definition: Lizard of Africa and Madagascar able to change skin color and having a projectile tongue.

monitor.definition: A large lizard with a long neck, strong limbs, and a long tail.

skink.definition: Alert agile lizard with reduced limbs and an elongated body covered with shiny scales.

bearded-dragon.definition: An Australian lizard with spiny scales around the throat that can form a beard-like display.
bearded-dragon.exampleUsage: The bearded dragon basked under the enclosure light.

anole.definition: Small arboreal tropical American insectivorous lizards with the ability to change skin color.
anole.exampleUsage: The anole was identified during the lesson.

komodo-dragon.definition: The world's largest living lizard, native to several Indonesian islands.
komodo-dragon.exampleUsage: The Komodo dragon walked across the protected habitat.

basilisk.definition: (classical mythology) a serpent (or lizard or dragon) able to kill with its breath or glance.

horned-lizard.definition: A broad-bodied lizard, mainly from North and Central America, with pointed scales or horns around the head.
horned-lizard.exampleUsage: The horned lizard blended with the sandy ground.

turtle.definition: A slow-moving animal with a hard shell.
turtle.exampleUsage: The turtle was identified during the lesson.

tortoise.definition: Usually herbivorous land turtles having clawed elephant-like limbs.

sea-turtle.definition: Large turtles that spend most of their lives in tropical or subtropical oceans come ashore mainly to lay eggs on sandy beaches.
sea-turtle.arabicTranslation: كائن أو عنصر طبيعي يُسمّى «سيا تورتلي»

snapping-turtle.definition: A large freshwater turtle with powerful jaws and a long tail, known for defensive snapping when threatened.
snapping-turtle.exampleUsage: Visitors observed the snapping turtle from outside the enclosure.

crocodile.definition: Large voracious aquatic reptile having a long snout with massive jaws and sharp teeth and a body covered with bony plates.
crocodile.exampleUsage: The crocodile was identified during the lesson.

alligator.definition: To crack and acquire the appearance of alligator hide, as from weathering or improper application.

caiman.definition: A semiaquatic reptile of Central and South America that resembles an alligator but has a more heavily armored belly.
caiman.exampleUsage: The caiman was identified during the lesson.

terrapin.definition: Any of various edible North American web-footed turtles living in fresh or brackish water.

softshell.definition: A freshwater turtle with a flattened body and a flexible leathery shell rather than a hard scaly shell.
softshell.exampleUsage: The softshell turtle rested on the sandy bottom.

gharial.definition: A long-snouted crocodilian native to rivers of the Indian subcontinent and adapted mainly for catching fish.
gharial.exampleUsage: The gharial swam through the deep section of the exhibit.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

shell.definition: A rigid covering that envelops an object.

fang.definition: An appendage of insects that is capable of injecting venom.
fang.exampleUsage: The fang was identified during the lesson.

tongue.definition: The muscular part of the mouth used for tasting, speaking, and swallowing.

tail.definition: The time of the last part of something.

claw.definition: Sharp curved horny process on the toe of a bird or some mammals or reptiles.
claw.exampleUsage: The claw was identified during the lesson.

eye.definition: Good discernment (either visually or as if visually).

jaw.definition: The part of the skull of a vertebrate that frames the mouth and holds the teeth.

skin.definition: A natural protective body covering and site of the sense of touch.

venom.exampleUsage: The venom was identified during the lesson.

terrarium.definition: A vivarium in which selected living plants are kept and observed.

heat-lamp.definition: An electric heater uses a powerful incandescent bulb to produce heat through invisible infrared radiation.

water-dish.definition: A shallow container kept filled with water so animals can drink from it.
water-dish.exampleUsage: The water dish was identified during the lesson.

branch.definition: A woody part that grows from a tree trunk or large branch.

rock.definition: A hard natural material found on the ground.

sand.definition: Small loose grains of rock or mineral material.

hide.definition: The dressed skin of an animal (especially a large animal).
hide.exampleUsage: The hide was identified during the lesson.

log.definition: A written record of messages sent or received.

misting-system.definition: An engineered setup that sprays tiny water droplets to control heat, moisture, or airborne particles in enclosed settings.

shed.definition: A small farm building used for storage or animals.
shed.exampleUsage: The shed was identified during the lesson.

bask.definition: To derive or receive pleasure from.

hunt.definition: An association of huntsmen who hunt for sport.

swim.definition: To move through water using the arms, legs, or body.

burrow.definition: To move through by or as by digging.

camouflage.definition: An outward semblance that misrepresents the true nature of something.

hiss.definition: To express or utter with a hiss.

strike.definition: A group's refusal to work in protest against low pay or bad work conditions.

coil.definition: A structure consisting of something wound in a continuous series of loops.
